prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 2017 manifesto (ideology-free)

Brexit and trade
- Six tests: restore full UK lawmaking and leave ECJ jurisdiction; full control of immigration/asylum and borders; regain a 200‑mile Exclusive Economic Zone and fishing policy; regain independent trade policy outside the single market and customs union; no “divorce” payment and recovery of UK shares in EU institutions; complete exit by end‑2019.
- Prefer rapid legal exit, repeal pre‑EU fishing accords, rebuild fisheries, end discards, license limited foreign access during transition, and require all fish caught in UK waters to be landed in the UK.

Public finances and tax
- Fund priorities by cutting foreign aid to 0.2% GNI, cancelling HS2, replacing the Barnett Formula with needs‑based funding, savings from leaving the EU, and other efficiencies.
- Cost‑of‑living: remove VAT from domestic energy and hot takeaway food; abolish TV licence via phased transition; cut green levies; remove VAT on sanitary products.
- Raise income tax personal allowance to £13,500 and 40% threshold to £55,000; raise inheritance tax threshold to £500,000 per person; pursue corporate tax avoidance.

Business and jobs
- 20% business rates cut for small premises; tackle late payments; open public procurement to SMEs; no quarterly tax returns for the self‑employed.
- Require jobs to be advertised in the UK first; allow preference for under‑25 UK applicants; protect minimum/living wage and curb exploitative zero‑hours use.

Housing
- Create a Housing Development Corporation to deliver up to 100,000 factory‑built modular homes annually on brownfield sites for first‑time buyers under 40, with resale back to the HDC at cost plus inflation. Tighten standards and enforcement against substandard rentals; review housing associations.

Health and social care
- Additional £11bn annually by 2021/22 (c.£9bn NHS, £2bn social care); integrate health and social care under one department.
- Expand medical and nursing training; fund GP growth; restore nursing bursaries; end hospital parking charges; license NHS managers; phase out PFI; ensure reciprocal charging and require insurance for non‑eligible users.

Mental health
- +£500m per year; 28‑day maximum wait; nationwide school counselling; improved perinatal and veteran mental health services.

Education and skills
- Grammar and technical schools expansion; German‑style dual vocational training; abolish KS1 SATs; restore maintenance grants; scrap tuition fees for STEM (with UK service) and for medical students (with NHS service); stronger careers and employability education; protect and expand SEND provision.

Elderly, disability, carers
- Maintain pensioner benefits and triple lock; +£2bn/year for social care; improve care workforce terms; dementia plan (+£400m/year); reform disability assessments; increase Carer’s Allowance and leave.

Immigration and integration
- Target net migration to balance over five years; points‑based and work‑permit system; five‑year moratorium on low‑skilled migration (with seasonal visas); 5‑year contributions before benefits/non‑urgent NHS; stricter family visas; guaranteed status for pre‑Article‑50 EU residents; no amnesty for illegal migrants.

Policing and justice
- +20,000 police, +7,000 prison officers; restore robust stop‑and‑search; reduce overcrowding; segregate prison extremists; tougher action on prison violence and drugs; tighter alcohol licensing; opt out of the European Arrest Warrant; UK Bill of Rights; stronger measures against FGM, forced marriage, “honour” crime; ban full‑face coverings in public.

Defence and veterans
- Spend at least 2% of GDP on defence plus +£1bn/year; increase armed forces by 20,000; retain nuclear deterrent; overhaul procurement; veterans’ administration, housing, jobs guarantees in police/prisons/border force; tax exemption while on overseas operations.

Transport
- Cancel HS2; upgrade existing rail, especially east‑west in the North; remove road tolls; support EV charging; diesel scrappage with EV/hybrid incentives; protect regional airports; freeze and aim to reduce Air Passenger Duty.

Environment, farming, animal welfare, energy
- New Environmental Protection Act; stronger protection for ancient woodland; greener planning (trees, permeable surfaces); bottle‑deposit review; prioritize brownfield.
- Replace CAP with a capped UK farm payment focused on active, smaller and hill farms; support antibiotic reduction.
- Ban live exports for fattening/slaughter; CCTV in abattoirs; clearer slaughter‑method labelling; tougher cruelty penalties.
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; leave Paris Agreement and EU ETS; pursue a mixed energy strategy including nuclear and shale (not in protected areas); cut domestic energy costs and unfair utility charges.

Democracy and local government
- Abolish the House of Lords; create an English Parliament; halve the Commons with proportional representation; citizen‑initiated binding referenda; tighten postal voting.
- Local referenda on major developments; restore committee governance; cut council waste and perks.
